title: refine: board-first top tabs + design search pill
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #364 (top-anchored navigation, now merged). Two refinements matching the shell bake-off's picked direction B:

1. **Top tabs read Board → People → On our hearts** — `/board` is now labeled **The Board** in navigation (the design's primary tab), ordered first for admins. The journey board's page heading "The Journey" stays as its own destination, per the reference's More menu.

2. **Search bar matches the design** — the topbar pill now reads `Search or jump to…` with an always-visible ⌘K hint. The palette already does everything: a role-aware "Go to" section listing every reachable destination, type-to-jump-by-name, quick actions, and shortcuts (⌘K / Ctrl+K).

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run lint` — 0 errors
- `npx vitest run` — 1656 passed; coverage thresholds met
- `npm run build` — succeeds

## Files

- `src/lib/permissions.ts` (`/board` nav label → "The Board")
- `src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` (placeholder + ⌘K hint)
- tests/e2e updated to the new label (`TopNav`, `permissions`, `GlobalSearch`, `e2e/permissions.spec.ts`), `CHANGELOG.md`

title: [Macro study] Expand the command palette + central shortcut registry
body:
Part of #325 · **Code**

## Problem

Keyboard handling is ad hoc and undiscoverable: `⌘K` in `GlobalSearch.tsx:295`, `⌘Enter` in `Thread.tsx`, `TodoComposer.tsx`, `LogVisitModal.tsx`, and `FeedbackFAB.tsx` — five separate listeners, no registry, nothing listed anywhere. The ⌘K palette offers four quick actions with no way to learn what else exists.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/` — a registry where every command declares its scope, description, condition, and handler, so the same registration both binds the key and populates the command palette. Shortcuts teach themselves.

## Explicitly NOT adopting

Their leader grammar (`c`+letter creates, `g`+letter goes) and vim navigation (`j`/`k`, `gg`, `shift+G`). Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day; this app serves students and Full-timers opening it a few times a week, often on a phone. Also skipping their priority chain and scope inheritance — far more machinery than this needs.

## Scope

- A small registry: id, scope, description, handler
- Both binds the shortcut and populates the ⌘K palette
- Migrate the five existing ad-hoc listeners onto it
- Palette lists available actions with their shortcuts

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every existing shortcut still works
- [ ] The palette lists actions the user can currently take, filtered by role
- [ ] Registering a command in one place makes it both bound and discoverable

title: [Macro study] Four new to-do creation entry points
body:
Part of #325 · **Code + light design**

## Problem

To-dos can be created from two places: highlighting a line on a Board page, and from an interaction. Macro's argument is that trackers go stale because logging costs a context switch — they made tasks creatable from seven places for exactly this reason.

## Scope — four new entry points

1. **From an attendance absence** — marking someone absent on the Gatherings screen is the exact moment someone thinks "I should check on them." Highest value of the four.
2. **From the visit log form** — `Visit.followUpTaskId` already exists in the data model, so this is wiring, not schema. Makes creating the follow-up part of writing the visit up rather than a separate step.
3. **From a chat message** — hover / long-press → "Make a to-do", carrying the message as source. Mirrors the Board highlight flow already built.
4. **From a prayer** — turn a burden into a concrete follow-up while keeping the prayer linked as source.

## Implementation note

One shared helper over `addTodo` in `src/lib/todos.ts`; each site differs only in which source it links. The existing `sourceDocId` / `sourceInteractionId` pattern extends naturally.

## Design needed

Small — the affordance in four placements. Reuse the existing "Make a to-do" treatment from the Board.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four create a to-do linked back to its source
- [ ] The source is visible on the resulting to-do row
- [ ] Available on mobile where the source screen exists

title: [Macro study] Role-aware first-run checklist
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

There is no first-run experience. New trainees arrive every semester, and the four roles (Full-timer / Trainee / Student / Community) see substantially different apps.

## What Macro does

`apps/web/src/features/getting-started/getting-started-types.ts` — a checklist where each row has an optional `isComplete()` read reactively from **live state**, plus `observe()` for event-driven completion, defaulting to "clicking it completes it". Their comment on why completion is derived rather than remembered:

> never persisted itself, so it stays honest when e.g. a tool is disconnected

## Scope

- Dismissible checklist on Home, rows differing per role
- Completion derived from real state — "logged your first conversation" is true because they did, not because they clicked a button once
- Collapsible sections, persisted per user

## Design needed

Checklist layout, per-role row sets, and copy for four roles in the app's existing voice.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each role sees rows relevant to what they can actually do
- [ ] Completion reads live state; deleting the underlying data un-completes the row
- [ ] Dismissible, and stays dismissed

title: [Macro study] Live contact pill with hover preview
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Attaching a contact to a message stores `ChatAttachment { type, id, name, subtitle }` — a display cache written at attach time. It goes stale, and checking one fact about the person means opening `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (2,402 lines).

## What Macro does

Every @mention renders as a live pill carrying its target's *current* metadata — a task pill shows the task's status and priority — and previews on hover. Context without a click, and the pill can't go stale because it reads live.

## Scope

- Contact pill showing stage and last-seen, read live rather than from the cached `subtitle`
- Hover preview card on desktop; tap-to-preview on mobile
- Contacts only for now; the other seven `ChatAttachment` types can follow if this lands well

## Design needed

Pill treatment (including stage colour, which already exists as `StageChip`) and the preview card.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pill reflects a stage change without the message being re-sent
- [ ] Preview shows enough to answer "who is this and where are they at" without opening the modal
- [ ] Works on mobile web and in `apps/mobile/`

title: [Macro study] One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · ⚠️ **Has a privacy consequence — read before designing**

## Problem

A conversation about one person can live in three places today:

1. `contacts/{id}/threads` — the walking-together thread (Trainee-visible)
2. The Comments tab in `ContactDetailsModal.tsx` (~line 2079) — gated `role === "admin" || isAdmin`, **Full-timers only**
3. Messages, with the contact attached via `ChatAttachment`

Someone asking "what did we say about Sarah?" has to check all three.

## What Macro does

*"Every deal gets its own channel, automatically, pinned right to the deal record."* Their argument: a CRM comment box always loses to where the conversation really happens, because people comment *and then* go ping the channel anyway. So the record's notes ARE the chat system, not a parallel one.

## ⚠️ Blocker — decide before this is designed

The Comments tab is Full-timer-only; the walking-together thread is Trainee-visible. **Merging them changes who can read pastoral oversight notes that were written under a different expectation.** This is a privacy change, not just a data migration. Pick one:

- **(recommended)** Migrated comments carry a visibility flag and the merged thread filters by role — preserves the original audience while still giving one place to look. Costs a `firestore.rules` change.
- Comments migrate into a Full-timer-only section of the merged thread.
- Existing comments stay in place; only *new* conversation goes to the thread.

## Scope

- `contacts/{id}/threads` becomes the single conversation surface
- Comments migrated per the decision above, with a migration script
- Attaching a contact in Messages links into that same thread rather than starting a parallel one
- `firestore.rules` updated and reproduced against the emulator **before** the rule is edited (rules deploys have their own CI gate — budget for it)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Visibility decision recorded in this issue before design starts
- [ ] No existing comment becomes readable by someone who could not read it before
- [ ] Emulator-backed rules tests, red before green
- [ ] Migration is reversible or dry-runnable

title: [Macro study] Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code**

## Problem

Row actions differ per view — the same intent is worded and placed differently on a person, a prayer, a visit, and a gathering. Users learn the app per screen instead of once.

## What Macro does

Defines an action vocabulary once and applies it to every object type — `apps/web/src/lib/core/hotkey/tokens.ts` has `entity.action.{markDone, markRead, delete, rename, share, favorite, createReminder, assignee, status, ...}`. Same key, same menu, same wording regardless of what the object is. Their keyboard reference has a single "Entity Actions" section covering all types.

## Scope

- Agree one action set — done, follow up later, share, make a to-do, open — and the exact wording, in the app's existing warm voice
- One row/overflow menu component consumed by person, prayer, visit, and gathering rows
- First consumer is the merged attention feed (#330), so co-design with it

## Design needed

The overflow menu, its trigger, and mobile (long-press drawer) treatment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One menu component used by all four row types
- [ ] "Done" means the same thing everywhere
- [ ] Wording reviewed against the existing nav voice ("The Journey", "On our hearts", "Looking back")

title: [Macro study] Notification stacking by target
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Pairs with #330

## Problem

`NotificationCenter.tsx` renders notifications flat. Three people commenting on one contact produces three rows, so the one thing that actually needed attention gets buried. This matters more here than in a workspace tool — notification volume per person is low, so a flat list is mostly noise around a few signals.

## What Macro does

Collapses all notifications about the same entity into a single row showing the most recent, with the rest behind a collapsible list (`DEFAULT_VISIBLE_COUNT = 3`), and lets you mark the whole stack read or done at once. See `apps/web/src/features/entity/extractors-notification/notification-stacks.tsx`.

## Scope

Group rows by target entity, show a count ("3 new on Sarah"), expand on demand, mark-all-done on the stack.

## Design needed

Stacked row treatment, count badge, expanded state.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Multiple notifications about one contact render as one row with a count
- [ ] Expanding shows the individual entries
- [ ] Mark-done on the stack clears all of them

title: [Macro study] Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
body:
Part of #325 · **Design + code** · Blocked on #326 (read/done model) and #327 (date bucketing)

## Problem

"What needs my attention" is split across three surfaces:

- My Day's hand-assembled sections (`src/views/MyDay.tsx`, 1,192 lines)
- `FromTraineesInbox` — the Full-timer oversight feed
- `NotificationCenter` — the bell, a separate list entirely

Someone has to check all three to know where they stand. And `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` only tracks *scanned*, which is passive — without a "done", the list only grows, so it stops being a list anyone can finish, and people stop opening it.

## What Macro does

One list holding email, messages, @mentions, task assignments, and agent results. `e` marks done and removes the item. Their framing: *"You can think of the Signal view as your action list."* The stance is that you should check exactly one thing.

**Not adopting:** their AI-sorted Signal/Noise split (volume doesn't justify it, and the failure mode — AI hides something pastoral — is worse than the problem), and Inbox-Zero-as-pressure. A list of people you haven't followed up with is not disposable the way email is; "clearing" a person is a strange verb, and a UI that rewards emptying the list can teach people to dismiss rather than follow up. Take *"done is distinct from seen"*; leave the pressure to reach zero.

## Scope

- One attention feed on My Day carrying team activity, to-do assignments, thread questions, and notifications
- Explicit per-row "done" that removes it, built on #326
- Date-group headers from #327
- Bell becomes push delivery only, not a second list

## Design needed

Row anatomy per item kind, the done affordance, group headers, empty state. Desktop, `MyDayMobile.tsx`, and `apps/mobile/`.

## Watch

The feed reads contacts, interactions, a `collectionGroup` over threads, notifications, and to-dos. My Day already does several of these — measure read volume before adding more, and check whether new composite indexes are needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One feed replaces the three surfaces; the bell no longer maintains a parallel list
- [ ] Marking done removes the row and persists per-user
- [ ] Each of the four roles sees an appropriate feed
- [ ] Firestore read count per load measured and recorded

title: [Macro study] Audit and derive Contact activity fields
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only**

## Problem

`Contact` carries `lastSeen`, `lastContactedDate`, `lastContactedBy`, `lastContactedById`, and `hasNewActivity`. All of these look derivable from interactions, visits, and attendance — but if any is hand-entered, or written at only some of the call sites, it goes stale silently. A stale `lastContactedDate` breaks exactly the question the app exists to answer: who have we not seen in a while.

## What Macro does

From their CRM docs: *"records create themselves … stages are all manual: Macro doesn't yet know where a company lies in your pipeline and relies on you."* A clean line between what the system can observe and what only a person knows. Their "Last Interaction" is a sortable column precisely because it is never typed.

Stage stays manual here too — that is judgment, and correctly a human's.

## Scope

1. Map every write of the five fields across web (`src/lib/`, `src/views/`, `src/components/modals/`) and `apps/mobile/`
2. Route them through one derived update triggered by logging an interaction, a visit, or an attendance mark
3. Remove any path that accepts them as direct user input

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Logging an interaction, a visit, and an attendance mark each update the fields identically
- [ ] No UI writes these fields directly
- [ ] Tests cover all three event types
- [ ] Audit findings recorded in the issue before the fix lands, so the size of the drift is known

title: [Macro study] Frecency ranking in Global Search
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · Highest value-per-line item in the study

## Problem

`src/components/layout/GlobalSearch.tsx` does substring filtering, caps each group at `GS_MAX = 4`, and applies **no ranking**. With no query, "recent people" sorts by `updatedAt` — which is *someone else's* edit, not your usage. So the people you open every day are not the people you are shown.

## What Macro does

`crates/frecency` computes, per user per entity:

```
frequency = log2(event_count + 2)
recency   = Σ over last 10 events of  exp(-0.1 × hours_ago) × weight
score     = 0.7 × frequency + 0.3 × recency

weights:  open = +2.0,  ping = 0.0,  close = -1.0
```

The negative close weight is the interesting part: opening something and immediately closing it is evidence it was the *wrong* result, so it demotes itself.

Their own client ships a much cheaper version for the command palette — `apps/web/src/features/command/recency.ts` is ~20 lines, a persisted `Record<commandId, timestamp>`. **That is the version to copy**, not the Rust service.

## Scope

- Track opens in a per-uid localStorage store, reusing the pub/sub pattern already in `src/lib/inboxReads.ts`
- Rank results by score; keep the substring filter as the gate (frecency only orders what already matched)
- Consider whether `GS_MAX = 4` should rise once ordering is meaningful

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a contact repeatedly floats it to the top of the no-query list
- [ ] Open-then-immediately-close does not promote a result
- [ ] Scoring is a pure function with unit tests; storage is tested separately

title: [Macro study] Unify read/done state into one per-user model
body:
Part of #325 · **Phase 1 — code only** · **Prerequisite for the merged attention feed**

## Problem

Five mechanisms currently answer fragments of one question — "has this person seen / dealt with this?":

- `src/lib/inboxReads.ts` — localStorage, per-uid, ids like `contact:<id>` (already an entity ref)
- `src/lib/convHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden conversations
- `src/lib/messageHides.ts` — localStorage, hidden messages
- `Notification.readBy` / `dismissedBy` — Firestore arrays
- `Contact.reviewed` — a boolean on the shared domain object

Three storage strategies, no shared vocabulary. `Contact.reviewed` is the worst of them: it puts a per-user workflow state onto a shared record, so when two Full-timers walk with the same trainee it is ambiguous who reviewed it.

## What Macro does

Separates two orthogonal axes and applies both uniformly to any entity: **read** (I have seen it) and **done** (I have dealt with it). `inboxReads` today only models "scanned", which is passive — there is no way to clear something off your list.

## Scope

- One per-user store keyed by entity ref (`contact:<id>`, `interaction:<id>`, `thread:<id>` — the shape `inboxReads.ts` already uses), with `read` and `done` as separate axes.
- Migrate `inboxReads`, `convHides`, `messageHides` behind it.
- Leave `Notification.readBy` alone for now — it is genuinely shared state, not a per-device preference.
- Plan the `Contact.reviewed` migration but do not remove the field in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Existing inbox-read and hide behaviour is unchanged from the user's point of view
- [ ] A `done` axis exists and is independently settable from `read`
- [ ] Unit tests cover set/clear/subscribe on both axes and the migration from each legacy store

title: [Macro study] Adopt product patterns from the Macro codebase (tracking)
body:
Tracking issue for work adopting product patterns from a read-only study of [macro-inc/macro](https://github.com/macro-inc/macro) (AGPLv3, SolidJS + Rust all-in-one workspace).

## Why

Macro's CRM, tasks, docs, and channels map closely onto People/The Journey, to-dos, Coordination Notes, and Messages. Their product decisions are stances rather than infrastructure, so they port even though none of their code does. Their core arguments:

- **Trackers go stale** because logging costs a context switch — so make creating an entry possible from wherever the decision is actually made.
- **Records should build themselves**; only judgment (stage) is manual.
- **You should check one thing** to know what needs your attention, and "done" must be a real verb distinct from "seen."
- **A record's notes ARE the chat system** — a separate comments box always loses to where the conversation really happens.

## Scaled down deliberately

Macro serves ~15 engineers living in the tool 8 hours a day. This app serves four roles who open it a few times a week, often on a phone. Keyboard-first navigation (vim keys, `c`/`g` leader grammar) was evaluated and **declined**; splits/window management, the filter AST, the properties system, and AI Signal/Noise sorting were also declined as poor fits.

## Scope multiplier

Every design-touching item lands in up to three places: the desktop view, its `*Mobile.tsx` twin (7 such pairs exist), and the React Native app in `apps/mobile/`. This is the main reason the code-only foundation goes first — it is written once and shared.

## Phase 1 — foundation, code only, unblocked

Nothing here needs design input; all four can proceed in parallel.

- [ ] #326 — Unify read/done state into one per-user model **(prerequisite for the merged feed)**
- [ ] #327 — Shared date bucketing util **(feeds the merged feed's grouping)**
- [ ] #328 — Frecency ranking in Global Search
- [ ] #329 — Audit and derive Contact activity fields

## Phase 2 — design assets

Merged attention feed · shared row action menu · contact pill + hover preview · merged thread tab · role-aware first-run checklist · four "Make a to-do" affordances.

## Phase 3 — build against the designs

- [ ] #330 — Merge attention surfaces into one feed with a done action
- [ ] #331 — Notification stacking by target
- [ ] #332 — Shared action vocabulary + shared row menu
- [ ] #333 — One conversation thread per person; retire the admin Comments tab ⚠️ **has a privacy decision to make first**
- [ ] #334 — Live contact pill with hover preview
- [ ] #335 — Role-aware first-run checklist
- [ ] #336 — Four to-do creation entry points
- [ ] #337 — Expand the ⌘K palette + central shortcut registry

## Testing

Per `CLAUDE.md` §6 all of this is logic/data/permissions code, so TDD is mandatory — failing test first. Coverage thresholds in `vitest.config.ts` ratchet up only.
